questions.stem: Two small balls with masses m and 2m are attached to both ends of a rigid rod of length d and negligible mass. If angular momentum of this system is L about an axis (A) passing through its centre of mass and perpendicular to the rod then angular velocity of the system about A is :
questions.solution:
m $\longleftarrow d \longrightarrow$ 2m
We know for two mass system, angular momentum is
$L = \mu d^{2}\omega$
reduced mass $= \frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1} + m_{2}}$
$L = \left(\frac{m \times 2m}{m + 2m}\right)d^{2}\omega$
$L = \frac{2}{3}md^{2}\omega$
$\omega = \frac{3L}{2md^{2}}$

questions.stem: A $20\ \mathrm{m}$ long uniform copper wire held horizontally is allowed to fall under the gravity ($g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^{2}}$) through a uniform horizontal magnetic field of $0.5$ Gauss perpendicular to the length of the wire. The induced EMF across the wire when it travells a vertical distance of $200\ \mathrm{m}$ is ________ mV.

In a screw gauge, the zero of the circular scale lies 3 divisions above the horizontal pitch line when their metallic studs are brought in contact. Using this instrument thickness of a sheet is measured. If pitch scale reading is $1\ \mathrm{mm}$ and the circular scale reading is 51 then the correct thickness of the sheet is ______ mm.
[Assume least count is $0.01\ \mathrm{mm}$]
questions.solution:
$|-\text{ve zero error}| = 3 \times L \cdot C$
$\text{Reading} = M \cdot S \cdot R + C \cdot C \times L \cdot C + |-\text{ve zero error}|$
$= 1\ \mathrm{mm} + 51 \times 0.01\ \mathrm{mm} + 3 \times 0.01\ \mathrm{mm}$
$= 1.54\ \mathrm{mm}$

A small bob A of mass m is attached to a massless rigid rod of length $1\ \mathrm{m}$ pivoted at point P and kept at an angle of $60^\circ$ with vertical as shown in figure. At distance of $1\ \mathrm{m}$ below point P, an identical bob B is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius R as shown in figure. If bob B just manages to complete the circular path of radius R upto a point Q after being hit elastically by bob A, then radius R is __________m.
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy of A just before striking B.
$mg(1 - 1\cos 60) = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
$\frac{mg}{2} = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$
$V = \sqrt{10}$
Due to elastic collision velocity gets transferred to ball (B)
For it to complete circle
$V = \sqrt{5gR}$
$\sqrt{10} = \sqrt{5gR}$
$\frac{1}{5} = R$

questions.stem: The moment of inertia of a square loop made of four uniform solid cylinders, each having radius R and length L ($R < L$) about an axis passing through the mid points of opposite sides, is (Take the mass of the entire loop as M) :
questions.solution:
Let mass of each rod is $M_{1}$
$I = \left(\frac{M_{1}R^{2}}{4} + \frac{M_{1}\ell^{2}}{12}\right) \times 2 \ldots$ for rod (1) & (2)
$\left(\frac{M_{1}R^{2}}{2} + \frac{M_{1}\ell^{2}}{4}\right) \times 2 \ldots$ for rod (3) & (4)
$I = \frac{3}{2}M_{1}R^{2} + \frac{2}{3}M_{1}\ell^{2}$
$= \frac{3}{2}\frac{M}{4}R^{2} + \frac{2}{3}\frac{M}{4}\ell^{2}$
$= \frac{3}{8}MR^{2} + \frac{M\ell^{2}}{6}$

questions.stem:
In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses $15\ \mathrm{kg}$ and $25\ \mathrm{kg}$, moving in opposite directions with speeds of $10\ \mathrm{m/s}$ and $30\ \mathrm{m/s}$, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in $^\circ\mathrm{C}$), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is :
(specific heat of sphere material $31\ \mathrm{cal/kg}\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $1\ \mathrm{cal} = 4.2\ \mathrm{J}$)
questions.solution:
$KE_{\text{lost}} = \frac{1}{2}\mu v_{r}^{2}(1 - e^{2})$
($\mu$ = reduced mass)
For $e = 0$
$\frac{1}{2}\mu v_{r}^{2} = 15c\Delta\theta + 25c\Delta\theta$
$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{15 \times 25}{15 + 25}(30 + 10)^{2} = 40 \times 31 \times 4.2\Delta\theta$
$\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{15 \times 25}{1} \times \frac{1}{31 \times 4.2} = \Delta\theta = 1.44$

Theory based

questions.stem: The de Broglie wavelength of an oxygen molecule at $27^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $x \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m}$. The value of x is (take Planck's constant $= 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, Boltzmann constant $= 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J/K}$, mass of oxygen molecule $= 5.31 \times 10^{-26}\ \mathrm{kg}$)

In hydrogen atom spectrum, ($R \rightarrow$ Rydberg's constant)
(A) the maximum wavelength of the radiation of Lyman series is $\frac{4}{3R}$
(B) the Balmer series lies in the visible region of the spectrum
(C) the minimum wavelength of the radiation of Paschen series is $\frac{9}{R}$
(D) the minimum wavelength of Lyman series is $\frac{5}{4R}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(i) Maximum wavelength Lyman series $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right), \ \lambda = \frac{4}{3R}$
(ii) Balmer lies in visible region
(iii) Minimum wavelength Paschen series $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{\infty}\right), \ \lambda = \frac{9}{R}$
(iv) Minimum wavelength Lyman series $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(1 - \frac{1}{\infty}\right), \ \lambda = \frac{1}{R}$

The equation of the electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating through free space is given by : $E = \sqrt{377}\sin(6.27 \times 10^{3}t - 2.09 \times 10^{-5}x)\ \mathrm{N/C}$. The average power of the electromagnetic wave is $\left(\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\mathrm{W/m^{2}}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
$\left(\text{Take } \sqrt{\frac{\mu_{0}}{\varepsilon_{0}}} = 377 \text{ in SI units}\right)$
questions.solution:
$\frac{Watt}{m^{2}} \Rightarrow$ Clearly it is asking about intensity
$I = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_{o}E_{0}^{2}C = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_{o}377\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_{0}\varepsilon_{0}}}$
$= \frac{1}{2}377\sqrt{\frac{\varepsilon_{0}}{\mu_{0}}} = \frac{377}{2} \times \frac{1}{377}$
$I = \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{\alpha}$
$\alpha = 2$
